description: The exactly-one-ledger-line law is delivered ONLY by the single-run finish_run door. The governed/concurrent batch functions (spawn_governed, spawn_concurrent) take no ledger parameter, return un-ledgerable IsolatedRun values (no LiveSpawn), and reap (kill) in-flight siblings on a hard failure of one run.
expected: Every spawned run — including one abandoned at orchestrator-teardown-while-in-flight or reaped during a governed-batch partial failure (a terminal cause enumerated in PLAN T-15.4-a) — yields exactly one ledger line, never zero, never silently absent.
observed: UNPROVEN in Epic-15's public surface: finish_run guarantees exactly-one-line per single run (proven green), but no batch/teardown path guarantees an aborted line for a reaped or abandoned in-flight run; those runs get zero ledger accounting. Confirmed by signature+return-type inspection (spawn_governed/spawn_concurrent have no ledger param and return IsolatedRun, not LiveSpawn).

description: The '12-14 concurrent runs on sandbox hardware' figure is a motivating reference under AD-13, never a validated budget; asserting it as a number would invent a perf claim (R-017).
expected: Only the min(cpu,memory) admission behaviour is testable and green; the concurrency count itself is not a pass criterion.
observed: UNPROVEN by design (structurally deferred): a validated budget needs an AD-13 fingerprinted baseline not reproducible in Epic-15 isolation. Recorded as a deliberate negative — no throughput/count literal is a gate; the governor also refuses to run without declared registry-key budgets.

description: Real OS-enforced hard memory-limit enforcement (Windows Job Object / POSIX rlimit) is not implemented; the watchdog OBSERVES peak working set and kills the OS process on breach.
expected: A per-run memory-limit breach produces a typed aborted refusal that kills the run.
observed: UNPROVEN / OS-conditional for the hard-cap facet: the portable gate — cooperative observed breach -> typed aborted -> kill — is proven green; a real OS-level hard cap (rlimit/Job Object) is neither set nor testable on this Windows host. The AC requirement (breach -> typed aborted) is otherwise satisfied.
